__readme: This file drives the GUI of the Room Config Builder. Edit it and press
'Reload Schema' in App Config (or restart the app) - no compile needed.
Each entry under 'fields' is keyed by a config.json property name and supports:
label:       Field label shown in the editor (defaults to the raw key).
labelWhen:   Condition -> label overrides, checked against the OTHER keys
in the same config block; the first match wins and none
matching falls back to 'label'. Conditions are 'key=value'
(equals) or 'key~text' (contains), case-insensitive. Used by
both the editor and the device report - e.g. input_usb reads
'VGA' when gui_usb_or_vga is VGA.
description: Text behind the (i) info button.
helperText:  Small grey hint line under the field.
type:        auto | text | int | double | bool | dropdown | combo | hidden | module_states.
'auto' (default) infers from the JSON value type.
options:     For dropdown/combo. Plain strings, or objects with value/label.
writes:      For combo only - the list of config keys the one dropdown writes.
Combo options use 'values' (one entry per key in 'writes').
moduleCommand: For module_states only - the command in the device's Python
module whose states become the options. Parsed live from the
module's self.Commands dictionary ('AllowedValues'), falling
back to the Set<Command> / __Match<Command> ValueStateValues.
addIfMissing: device_fields only - render the field on matching device tabs
even when the key does not exist in that device block yet;
the first edit writes it into config.json.
Keys may contain '*' wildcards (e.g. 'power1_outlet_*') to cover a whole
family of properties. Exact keys always win over wildcard matches.
Keys starting with '__' are ignored (use them for comments).
DEVICE-TYPE SCOPING: the top-level 'device_fields' object holds entries that
apply ONLY to matching config sections, keyed by a section pattern like
'PROJECTORDEVICE_*'. Scoped entries override the global 'fields' entries for
those device tabs - so a projector-only setting (or a projector-specific take
on a shared key like 'input') ships by editing this file, no recompile.
DEVICE DEFAULTS: the top-level 'device_defaults' object maps section patterns
to property/value pairs merged into every NEWLY CREATED device block of that
type (when the Setup Wizard counts change). Existing/template values are
never overwritten - only missing keys are added. Exact section names (e.g.
'SWITCHERDEVICE_1') override wildcard patterns per property, so switcher 1
can carry the audio groups while extra switchers stay clean.
DEVICE TYPES: the top-level 'device_types' object lists the device families
the Setup Wizard manages - each SYSTEM_SETUP dev_ count key mapped to its
section 'prefix' (required) and wizard 'label'. This list REPLACES the
built-in one, so keep every family you want here; the order here is the
wizard's display order. Adding an entry gives the new family a wizard count
dropdown, device tabs, export pruning, count audits, and a '0' default on
load. Pair it with 'fields'/'device_fields' entries for its properties and
'device_defaults' for its baseline values. Optional per-family extras:
max:                 highest count the wizard offers (default 8).
keepAlivePreference: command names tried in order when auto-picking a
new device's keep_alive_command from its module.
template:            full block for new devices when the config has no
<PREFIX>1 block to copy (else a basic one is built).
SYSTEM DEFAULTS: the top-level 'system_defaults' object holds the
SYSTEM_SETUP values injected into loaded configs that are missing them
(the migration step). Defining it REPLACES the built-in set. The dev_
counts are NOT listed here - every device_types family is always
injected as '0' automatically.
RUNTIME KEYS: the top-level 'runtime_written' list names config items the
PROCESSOR maintains itself while the room runs (the power schedule times,
ENVIRONMENT.traceback_allowed). A downloaded config carries them even
though the template never did, so they are skipped by the template audit
and are not drawn as unknown keys. Entries are 'SECTION' or 'SECTION.key'
with '*' wildcards.
CONSISTENCY: the top-level 'consistency' list cross-checks keys that have
to agree - when one condition holds, another must too. Violations never
block an edit or a save; they paint the red mismatch outline on every
field the rule flags so the tech can see both sides and fix the wrong one.
See the '__readme' inside that list for the entry format.
STANDALONE SECTIONS: config blocks that are neither SYSTEM_SETUP nor a
numbered device (e.g. 'METRICS_CONFIG') are rendered on the System tab as
their own group, below System Settings. Describe their properties under
the top-level 'section_fields' object (same entries as 'fields', keyed by
section name), give the group its heading with a normal 'fields' entry
named after the section, and list the baseline properties under
'section_defaults' - those are created/filled on load just like the
SYSTEM_SETUP migration, and are what 'Check Defaults' offers for the
group when the template config has no such block.
The wizard's device families. 'prefix' is the config section prefix the
numbered blocks use (PROJECTORDEVICE_1, ...); 'label' is the wizard text.
'max' caps the wizard count dropdown. 'keepAlivePreference' lists the
keep-alive commands to try (in order) when a new device's module is
parsed; if none match, 'Power'-style commands are used as before.
SYSTEM_SETUP values injected on load when missing (shown in the
acknowledgement dialog). Edit values here and press Reload Schema.
Whole non-device config blocks injected on load when missing (section
and/or individual properties), shown in the acknowledgement dialog.
ENVIRONMENT is deliberately NOT listed: traceback_allowed is opt-in per
room, so a conversion never turns it on. Add the block by hand when a
room needs it - the device report then states that it is allowed.
METRICS_CONFIG ships enabled with the bearer token filled in, so every
converted room reports metrics without a follow-up edit. The token is
what makes that safe: the processor's Metrics client raises at startup
when 'enabled' is true and 'bearer' is empty, so never blank the bearer
while leaving 'enabled' true. New configs built from the template get
the template's own values instead.

runtime_written: __readme: Config items the PROCESSOR writes into config.json while the room runs, so a downloaded file carries them even though the template never did. Listed here they are not reported by the template audit and not drawn as unknown keys on the System tab. Entries are SECTION or SECTION.key; * matches any run of characters.

__readme: Cross-key checks: when 'when' holds in a section, 'expect' must hold
too, or every field named in 'flag' gets the red mismatch outline and
'message' as its helper line. Conditions are 'key=value' (equals) or
'key~text' (contains), case-insensitive; '{key}' in a message inserts
that key's live value. Optional 'section' (default SYSTEM_SETUP)
accepts a '*' wildcard. Nothing is blocked or auto-corrected - the
tech sees both fields flagged and decides which one is wrong.
Entries without 'when' and 'expect' are skipped, which is what lets
this comment sit in the list. Defining any rule here REPLACES the
built-in set, so keep every rule you want in this array.

__readme: Baseline properties per device type, applied when the wizard creates the
blocks. Edit the values here and press Reload Schema - no recompile.
Field definitions scoped to one device type. The outer key is a pattern
matched against the config section name (e.g. PROJECTORDEVICE_1); the
inner entries use exactly the same properties as 'fields' above.

input.label: Input
input.description: Input the projector subscribe status follows. The options are read live from the selected Python module's 'Input' command dictionary, so only states that module actually supports are offered (manual typing still allowed).

__readme: Field definitions for standalone (non-device) config blocks, keyed by
section name. Same entry format as 'fields'; these win over the global
'fields' entries inside that section, so short property names like
'enabled' or 'uri' can be described per block without colliding.
Only the properties present in the block are rendered - the optional
tuning keys below are described here so they get a proper editor when
someone adds them by hand in the Raw JSON tab.

enabled.label: Metrics Enabled (enabled)
enabled.helperText: Needs a URI and a bearer token before it is turned on
enabled.description: Start the python metrics client (modules/project/metrics_client.py) on the processor. When false, a no-op DummyMetrics stands in and nothing is sent. WARNING: with this true and 'bearer' blank, the processor raises at startup - fill in the URI and token first.

keylogger.label: Log UI Events (keylogger)
keylogger.description: Send a metric for most touch panel events (button presses and the like) on top of the system's own metrics. Button releases and slider drags are skipped by the processor for performance.

uri.label: Metrics Ingest URI (uri)
uri.description: Full URL the processor POSTs batched metrics to, e.g. http://cts-metrics1:41796/metrics. Points at the AV-System-Metrics ingest service.

bearer.label: Bearer Token (bearer)
bearer.description: Secret sent as the 'Authorization: Bearer ...' header on every metrics POST. The ingest service rejects the batch without it, and the client refuses to start when it is blank.

batch_size.description: OPTIONAL. Metrics are sent once this many are queued (processor default 20). Also the maximum number sent per request.

flush_interval.description: OPTIONAL. Seconds to wait before sending a partial batch (processor default 10), so a quiet room still reports.

max_cache_size.description: OPTIONAL. Most metrics held in memory while the ingest server is unreachable (processor default 250). Must be >= batch_size. Oldest entries are dropped only once the failure thresholds below are passed.

failure_drop_message_threshold.description: OPTIONAL. Failed messages tolerated before the cache is allowed to drop its oldest entries (processor default 100).

failure_drop_time_threshold.description: OPTIONAL. Seconds of continuous send failures before the cache is allowed to drop its oldest entries (processor default 300).

request_timeout.description: OPTIONAL. Seconds to wait on the HTTP POST before treating it as failed (processor default 10).

send_heartbeat.description: OPTIONAL. Send the periodic 'Heartbeat' metric used to track room uptime (processor default true).

traceback_allowed.label: Allow Tracebacks (traceback_allowed)
traceback_allowed.description: Let the processor report full Python tracebacks when something raises, instead of swallowing the detail. Opt-in per room: a conversion never adds the ENVIRONMENT block, and the device report calls the setting out whenever the room does carry it.

morning_power_on_time.label: Morning Power-On Time (morning_power_on_time)
morning_power_on_time.description: Set by the PROCESSOR, not by hand: the time it next brings the room up, written back into config.json as the schedule shifts. Shown here for reference — editing it is overwritten on the next cycle.

nightly_shutdown_time.label: Nightly Shutdown Time (nightly_shutdown_time)
nightly_shutdown_time.description: Set by the PROCESSOR, not by hand: the time it next shuts the room down, written back into config.json as the schedule shifts. Shown here for reference — editing it is overwritten on the next cycle.

btn_name.description: GUI object name for the connection status that has two states. Usually represented as a red dot when disconnected.

com_type.description: Type of connection as a string (Serial, SerialOverEthernet, Network).

host.description: The processor or spdevice in use for serial connections.

relay_host.description: The processor in use for the relay power control.

device_id.description: The ID to be sent to the device if it is required.

gve_id.description: String that identifies the device in GVE. Needs to be created when you add the room devices to GVE.

input.description: Input for the device. The subscribe status will change to this input. (Examples: HDBaseT, HDMI 1, Digital Link).

ip_address.description: IP address for the device as a string.

keep_alive_command.description: Command as a string to send to the device once connected. Chosen from the dictionary of commands in the module.

keep_alive_interval.description: Timing for sending the keep_alive_command as an integer.

keep_alive_qualifier.description: Only needed if the command requires a qualifier (Example checking an audio group such as '1' as the qualifier).

lbl_name.description: Name for the GUI object that will be written for connection status.

manual_disconnect.description: Flag to disconnect the item. Used if a projector or item is temporarily removed from a room.

model.description: Model of the device. Picking a model from the dropdown switches 'module' to that model's default python file and applies the module's DEVICE_INFO connection + standard defaults (protocol, port, keep-alive, input, ...). The list is built from each module's DEVICE_INFO "models" list (falling back to its self.Models keys) and is filtered to this tab's device family via DEVICE_INFO "device_type"; the browse dialog can show all types.

keep_alive_trigger.description: Delay the keep_alive_command until the trigger is received such as the APC needing to complete the login before polling.

default_cc_aud_cam.description: Make the system show the audience camera as the capture source on startup.

gui_capture_source_available.description: Determine if the user can change the capture source on the touch panel.

gui_usb_or_vga.description: Set the GUI and metrics to send over the USB or VGA depending on the age of the room.

ntp_primary.description: Network Time Protocol (NTP) primary server address in use for the processor.

ntp_secondary.description: Network Time Protocol (NTP) secondary server address in use for the processor.

output_audio_ald.description: Output for the Assisted Listening Device in use for the room.

pcmac.description: Future use for the mac address on the local PC.

gui_demo_mode.description: Operate the touch panel while not connecting to any device.

module.description: File path to the module as a string.

name.description: Name of the device as it will appear in the logger.

net_port.description: Network Port used to send communications on network connected devices.

protocol.description: Protocol in use for network connections (TCP, SSH, or UDP).

serial_port.description: Serial port in use if using Serial as the com type.

service_port.description: Port for the response from the device. 0 is automatically assigned by the processor.

use_device_mute.description: Boolean for whether a mute command will also call to the device when video mute is pressed.

user.description: Username for the device when using a network connection.

password.description: Password in use while using a network connection that requires authentication.

active_debug_server.description: Event space timer (6hrs for inactivity shutdown, default is 3hrs) and the debug server can be enabled with this boolean.

active_event_space.description: Event space timer (6hrs for inactivity shutdown, default is 3hrs) and the debug server can be enabled with this boolean.

active_notifications.description: Notifications can be enabled with true or disabled with false.

disable_inactivity_timer.label: Disable Inactivity Timer (disable_inactivity_timer)
disable_inactivity_timer.helperText: Not a true disable - it pushes the shutdown out to 25hrs
disable_inactivity_timer.description: Selects the 'disabled' inactivity mode: the warning/shutdown timers move out past a full day (25hrs) so a multi-day event is never shut down on the presenter. Works with active_event_space (normal 3hr / event 6hr / disabled 25hr); this flag wins. The room's Timer button cycles the modes and saves both flags back into config.json on the processor.

use_qos.label: Use QoS Scheduler (use_qos)
use_qos.description: Route device Set/Update traffic through the quality of service scheduler (modules/project/quality_of_service.py) instead of firing every command the moment it is raised. Commands are queued by priority (high / low / lossy) and drained on a 100ms tick, so bursts of polling cannot starve what the user just pressed. False sends everything immediately, as older systems did.

active_reboot_listener.label: Reboot Listener (active_reboot_listener)
active_reboot_listener.description: Run the standalone TCP reboot listener (modules/project/reboot_listener.py) so the CTS Dashboard - or anything that can open a socket - can reboot the processor and the touch panels. Independent of active_debug_server: it has its own port and runs with the debug server switched off. False skips the listener entirely and the room can only be rebooted on site.

reboot_listener_port.label: Reboot Listener Port (reboot_listener_port)
reboot_listener_port.description: TCP port the reboot listener binds. Must not collide with the debug server or any other service on the processor. The CTS Dashboard has to be pointed at this port.

reboot_listener_interface.label: Reboot Listener Interface (reboot_listener_interface)
reboot_listener_interface.description: Which processor network interface the reboot listener binds to. Keep it on LAN unless the dashboard reaches the processor over the AV LAN.

reboot_listener_token.label: Reboot Listener Token (reboot_listener_token)
reboot_listener_token.helperText: Blank = no token check; set one for anything off a trusted VLAN
reboot_listener_token.description: Shared secret required in front of every plain-text command line (e.g. '<token> reboot processor'), and required somewhere in a debug client's handshake. Blank disables the check, which leaves the listener open to anyone who can reach the port.

reboot_listener_client_password.label: Reboot Listener Debug Password (reboot_listener_client_password)
reboot_listener_client_password.helperText: Blank = the stock debug password shipped with the template
reboot_listener_client_password.description: Handshake password for the debug-client protocol on the reboot listener's port - the part that makes the debugger's Reboot buttons work by changing only the port. Blank means the processor falls back to the stock DebugServer password, which is a constant in the template source, so set this AND a token for anything reachable off a trusted VLAN.

METRICS_CONFIG.label: Metrics (Python Metric Tracking)
METRICS_CONFIG.__comment: Not a property - this names the METRICS_CONFIG group heading on the System tab. Its properties live under 'section_fields'.
METRICS_CONFIG.description: Metric tracking for the python side: the processor batches events (system start/stop, device connects, UI presses) and POSTs them to the ingest service. Converted rooms get it enabled with the bearer token already filled in.

ENVIRONMENT.__comment: Not a property - this names the ENVIRONMENT group heading on the System tab. Its properties live under 'section_fields'.

power1_outlet_*.__comment: One wildcard entry covers power1_outlet_1 through power1_outlet_8.

power1_outlet_*_action.description: If you need to have the outlet set to reboot, use this action command to have the outlet only allow that action.
power1_outlet_*_action.__comment: More specific pattern listed after the generic one, so it wins for the _action keys.

power1_outlet_*_supports_reboot.description: Whether this outlet's hardware can power-cycle on command. Optional — a room without the key behaves as before. Set false for an outlet that must only be switched on or off (a screen relay, a device that dislikes a hard cycle).
power1_outlet_*_supports_reboot.helperText: Optional. Leave unset for rooms that don't use reboot control.
power1_outlet_*_supports_reboot.__comment: Listed after the generic power1_outlet_* entry: patterns are matched in reverse file order, so the more specific one wins.

power1_outlet_*_reboot_only.description: Whether reboot is the ONLY action this outlet offers — the GUI hides plain on/off for it. Optional; needs power1_outlet_N_supports_reboot to be true to mean anything.
power1_outlet_*_reboot_only.helperText: Optional. Reboot is the only action offered for this outlet.
power1_outlet_*_reboot_only.__comment: Listed after the generic power1_outlet_* entry: patterns are matched in reverse file order, so the more specific one wins.

relay_port_*.description: Relay port on the processor used for screen control (e.g. RLY1). _up raises the screen, _down lowers it, _stop halts travel.

group_*.description: Audio group number on the switcher/DSP. Set these in DSP Configurator / PCS, or the third-party device's software (e.g. Yamaha MTX Editor).
group_*.__comment: Wildcard fallback: exact group_ entries above still win where defined.

auto_reconnect.description: Automatically re-establish the connection to the device (e.g. ShareLink) if it drops.

startup_watchdog_stage.description: Top-level counter used by the processor's startup watchdog to track boot progress/retries. Managed by the running system - normally leave at 0.

__comment: TEMPLATE: to support a new config.json property, copy this block,

__example_new_key.label: My New Feature
__example_new_key.description: Explain what this new key does here.
